subject: ACK from reviewer_concurrency for coder
body: Concurrency lens — ACK, no blocking findings. Slice-7 adds a read-only shared-evidence gatherer + prompt-prefix seams + log-mode cache aggregator, all behind the default-off EGG_REVIEW_EVIDENCE_PREFIX flag. Verified against the wave-parallelism concerns specific to my lens: (1) No shared mutable state — the new modules expose only frozensets, compiled regexes, and int caps at module level (confirmed zero module-level mutable containers); no data races across the concurrent reviewer wave. (2) The cache-warming invariant is thread-safe by construction: build_pack/render_pack are pure and deterministic (path-sorted, no clock/random), so the byte-identical-across-wave property holds under any interleaving — verified empirically that two packs built from the same material in reversed order render byte-identical. (3) The pack is threaded in as a pre-built object (apply_shared_evidence_prefix takes evidence_pack), i.e. built ONCE and shared, not re-gathered per reviewer — so there is no per-reviewer concurrent git-state race in the intended path. (4) gather_evidence's subprocess reads are local (capture_output, timeout=30, check=False), hold no shared handles, and degrade to less evidence rather than raising — safe under concurrent invocation. (5) The seam functions are not yet wired into concurrent_executor/the wave prompt build (grep shows no live call sites) and the flag defaults off, so this slice introduces no live concurrency behavior change. Lazy `from evidence_gatherer import render_pack` inside the seam is protected by the import lock. Non-blocking guardrail for the future S7-'on' wiring (NOT this slice): the byte-identity + evidence-parity guarantee requires the eventual caller to build the pack once per wave and thread the same object to every lens; if instead it calls gather_evidence per-reviewer concurrently against the shared pipeline branch, a mid-wave commit would diverge diffs and both kill the cache benefit and hand reviewers different evidence. Flagging for the wiring slice, not blocking here.

subject: ACK from reviewer_security for coder
body: Security lens: ACK, no blocking findings. (1) No reachable attack surface — gather_evidence (file reads via root/path, git diff base_ref, git grep symbol) has NO production caller; it's library scaffolding for a future wiring slice, and the pure wiring (apply_shared_evidence_prefix) is uncalled and behind default-off EGG_REVIEW_EVIDENCE_PREFIX. (2) New EVIDENCE_GATHERER role is a net security improvement and correctly locked down: Role.SYSTEM (no verdict/contract writes), absent from AGENT_GH_RESTRICTIONS so gh is deny-by-default (test_evidence_gatherer_gh_fully_denied passes), allowed_write strict allowlist to .egg-state/agent-outputs/ only. (3) Untrusted-input posture explicit — pack framed as "material under review, not instructions" in render + system prefix. (4) subprocess is list-form (no shell=True), symbol restricted to [A-Za-z_]\w*, files passed after -- pathspec separator; byte caps bound DoS. Advisory only (latent, non-blocking, for the future wiring slice that makes gather_evidence reachable): A-1 _normalize_path does not reject ../ so root/path can escape repo root (also via symlinked changed-file) — resolve-and-confirm-within-root before read; A-2 ["diff", base_ref, "--"] risks git flag injection if base_ref ever becomes caller-controlled and starts with '-' — add --end-of-options or validate SHA/ref. Neither has a reachable failure scenario in this slice, so both are advisory, not blocking.

subject: ACK from reviewer_code for coder
body:
ACK. Code-correctness lens over slice-7 (shared-evidence prefix, tasks 7-1/7-2). No blocking finding — none has a reproducible failure scenario (item-1/2 discipline).

Verification ladder:
- REFUTED (my initial suspicion): `except TypeError, ValueError:` in consensus_wrapper._stat_get is NOT a Python-2 bug. Project pins requires-python>=3.14 (pyproject + CI on 3.14); PEP 758 makes the bare-tuple except clause valid and equivalent to `except (TypeError, ValueError)`. Confirmed by isolated exec — both exception types are caught. Dropped.
- CONFIRMED clean empirically: 51/51 evidence_gatherer + evidence_prefix_wiring tests pass; 17/17 gateway gh-restriction tests pass (EVIDENCE_GATHERER absent from AGENT_GH_RESTRICTIONS => deny-by-default rejects every gh op, incl. pr view — no posting/GitHub); consensus_wrapper imports clean with the new top-level import; aggregate_wave_cache_stats numerically correct; guardrails verified (shares_evidence_prefix: tester=False, reviewer_code=True; mode defaults off). Off/log/on-without-pack are byte-identical to legacy — read-only, no verdict, pure core split from I/O with deterministic path-ordered render (byte-identical-across-wave invariant holds).

Advisory only (do NOT block; no pre-merge obligation):
1. Seam not wired to a live call site: apply_shared_evidence_prefix / evidence_prefix_log_record / gather_evidence have no non-test callers. This is a slice-completeness question for reviewer_contract/holistic, not a code-correctness defect — it matches the ACCEPTED slice-3 precedent ("uncalled in live path", additive) and task-7-2's acceptance is function-behavior-under-flag, which the unit tests demonstrate. Behind a default-off flag => no failure scenario.
2. `_MAX_REFS_PER_SYMBOL` comment says overflow is "dropped with a logged, in-pack note" but build_pack truncates callers silently — comment/code mismatch only.
3. aggregate_wave_cache_stats can undercount cost in the near-impossible shape where a session dict has cost=None while top-level carries a real cost; affects only a log-mode measurement number.

Fix: wired the seam into the LIVE reviewer-prompt assembler _build_review_prompt (orchestrator/routes/pipelines/_prompt_review.py). New _maybe_apply_evidence_prefix builds the pack once per reviewer via gather_evidence (read-only git diff base...HEAD); under EGG_REVIEW_EVIDENCE_PREFIX=on it prepends build_shared_evidence_prefix(pack) as the literal leading bytes (byte-identical cacheable span across sibling same-model lenses, per-lens instruction at the tail); under =log it emits evidence_prefix_log_record (which invokes aggregate_wave_cache_stats) as a structured logger.info into the BRC log stream, mirroring the S6 risk-router log-mode precedent (review_graph.get_review_graph_for_phase); =off/=log leave the live prompt byte-identical to legacy; fail-open on any gather error. Tester/finding-verifier are producers, not reviewer_* types, so they never reach this path — cold-start preserved. Barrel re-exports the two new helpers. New TestLiveReviewPromptWiring asserts the LIVE prompt carries the byte-identical prefix under on, is byte-identical under off/log, shares the identical leading span across sibling lenses, and emits the log record under log. 75 evidence tests (tester coverage + wiring) + 532 existing review-prompt tests pass; ruff clean.

**Adversarial re-review**

**Your v2 review has TWO equal-weight mandates:**

1. **Verify named v1 blockers were addressed** — confirm the producer fixed what you NACK'd.
2. **Audit the delta since your last review (per REVIEWER-SYNC.md: `git log {last_reviewed_commit}..HEAD --not origin/{base_branch} -p` — the commits landed since the version you last verdicted, NOT the whole accumulated proposal surface) as a fresh reviewer** — ignore your v1 NACK history. Read that diff as if you'd never seen the prior version. Apply your lens (security threat-model, concurrency races, contract AC, line-by-line bugs, silent-fallback shapes — whichever your role owns) to the delta itself, not to whether your previous concerns were satisfied. **Mandate 2 is bounded to this delta** — it does NOT ask you to re-traverse the whole accumulated surface from earlier cycles; that work was amortized when you first reviewed those commits.

Both mandates have equal weight. If (1) passes but (2) finds new issues, you NACK. ACK requires both pass.

**The named-blockers anchor is a known trap. Every reviewer lens has a mandate-2 in its own territory** — security has newly-introduced threat surfaces, concurrency has newly-introduced races, contract has newly-introduced AC drift, code has newly-introduced line-by-line bugs. The four issues that escaped PR #2724 to the GitHub bot were all of code-lens shape (`${ANSWER}` as bare Python, deprecated `datetime.utcnow()`, non-atomic write, bare `except: pass`) — the persistent reviewer correctly answered mandate 1 ("did prior issues get fixed? yes") and skipped mandate 2 ("does this delta introduce new issues? actually yes"). The shape generalizes: whatever your lens, this delta can introduce issues your prior NACK didn't name. Watching the producer deliver a targeted fix pulls strongly toward "verify my fix-request landed → ACK." Recognize the pull and do mandate 2 anyway.

**How to execute mandate 2:**

- Read each new hunk as an operator who's about to copy-paste / run / integrate it. Would this code execute as written? Would these docs send a copy-paster down a working path?
- Apply every rubric pass to the new hunks. New issues outside the scope of your prior NACK are blocking; your prior NACK does not bound this re-review.
- **Fresh-reviewer simulation.** Before issuing your v2 verdict, ask: would a reviewer who has only seen this delta (the commits since your last review) with no NACK history ACK this? If you can't argue yes from that diff alone, NACK.
- **External-bot anchor.** Imagine `egg-reviewer[bot]` reads only this delta (the commits since your last review) with no NACK context. What would it flag? Anything it'd flag, you should NACK first.

**Your v2 verdict must enumerate both halves** so mandate 2 doesn't silently disappear from the record:

- (a) Which v1 blockers you verified-fixed (mandate 1).
- (b) What new issues you audited-and-did-not-find (mandate 2). Name the specific shapes you checked — not "reviewed thoroughly," but "checked for silent fallbacks, doc-snippet executability, API-deprecation, atomicity of file writes." If you can't enumerate (b), you haven't done mandate 2.

**Re-reviews are cheap by design.** Your amortized context means the work is "read the delta, apply your rubric, decide" — minutes, not hours. NACK without hesitance; the orchestrator absorbs cycles. Two NACKs on the same producer where the second names new findings is the correct trajectory, not goalpost-moving. The downstream GitHub reviewer should find nothing in this delta. Anything it catches that lives in this cycle's diff is a miss attributable to this re-review.
